articles.title: Muere el ‘Tyson Ruso’ a los 40 años tras una carrera truncada por un misterioso accidente en el metro de Berlín
articles.standfirst: El prometedor Denis Boytsov apareció gravemente herido en una vía de metro en 2015 y perdió la capacidad de andar y hablar
articles.summary: El prometedor Denis Boytsov apareció gravemente herido en una vía de metro en 2015 y perdió la capacidad de andar y hablar
articles.body: El mundo del boxeo está de luto tras conocerse el fallecido del exboxeador ruso Denis Boytsov a los 40 años. La causa de la muerte, según informó el centro deportivo regional de Oriol (Rusia), su ciudad natal, fue un coágulo de sangre, si bien Boytsov llevaba 11 años incapacitado. El ruso, que desarrolló toda su carrera en Alemania, fue considerado en su momento uno de los mayores talentos mundiales del peso pesado. En su mejor momento, Boytsov se convirtió en un potencial aspirante al título mundial de Wladimir Klitschko, pero su carrera terminó tras un grave accidente en Berlín en 2015, cuyas circunstancias nunca quedaron claras. Con un récord de 36-1 (27 KOs), el púgil obtuvo el apodo del ‘Tyson ruso’ debido a su potente golpeo (ganó por KO 18 de sus primeras 20 peleas), a su forma de boxear y a que físicamente era de un corte similar al de ‘Iron Mike’. Llegó a ser campeón Intercontinental de la WBA y segundo clasificado de las listas de este organismo, por lo que se le propuso como aspirante al título de Klitschko. En aquellos años de ascenso llegó a barajarse también un combate contra el emergente Tyson Fury. En realidad, estuvo a una pelea de luchar por el título mundial, pero en noviembre de 2013 Boytsov perdió contra Alex Leapai (decisión unánime con dos derribos) en una eliminatoria mundialista y ahí retrocedió varias casillas. Hizo tres combates posteriormente que poco a poco lo encaminaron de nuevo hacia su propósito, pero entonces sufrió un extraño accidente. En 2015, Boytsov fue encontrado inconsciente y gravemente herido en las vías de un túnel del metro de Berlín, entre dos estaciones. Su apartamento estaba a tan solo unos cientos de metros. El joven, que entonces tenía 29 años, fue trasladado de urgencia al hospital con graves lesiones en la cabeza y las manos. Allí fue sometido a una intervención de emergencia y posteriormente se le indujo un coma. Aquello dejó a Denis incapacitado para caminar y hablar. Las graves consecuencias de sus lesiones marcaron su vida desde ese momento. Aún no está claro cómo llegó al túnel del metro. La esposa de Boytsov, Olga, temió que su marido hubiera sido víctima de una venganza, pero tras analizar las declaraciones de los testigos y las grabaciones de vídeo, la policía de Berlín consideró que se trató de un accidente. No hubo pruebas de la participación de terceros en este incidente y la policía concluyó que Boytsov había sufrido sus lesiones de forma accidental mientras se encontraba en estado de embriaguez. Boytsov pasó siete semanas en coma inducido médicamente antes de comenzar su recuperación, si bien las secuelas neurológicas fueron muy graves. Se sometió a años de rehabilitación en Alemania antes de regresar a Rusia.

articles.title: Dana White Dismisses Rumors of UFC Saudi Arabia Event Being Rescheduled Amid Tensions in the Middle East
articles.summary: Dana White has confirmed that the UFC's event schedule is set to go as planned despite attacks and regional violence in Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
Growing security concerns in the Middle East have cast doubt over several major combat sports events scheduled in the region. Recent missile and drone attacks targeting critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, have raised questions about whether upcoming sporting events can proceed as planned.

According to DW News, Ansar Allah, the Yemeni movement commonly known as the Houthis, has repeatedly targeted Riyadh airport . The report cited an October 10 attack that killed 12 people and injured around 300, adding to concerns about security in the region.

The uncertainty has also put the UFC's rumored December 5 Fight Night in the spotlight. The card is expected to feature Israel Adesanya against Shara Magomedov, but speculation has emerged that the event could be canceled or moved elsewhere. Dana White , however, has offered a different outlook, suggesting the UFC is still moving ahead with its plans for the Middle East.

Dana White Says UFC Has No Plans to Alter Its Upcoming Fight Schedule

The December 5 card is not the only UFC event attracting attention amid the regional tensions. UFC 333 is scheduled for October 24 in Abu Dhabi, where Alexander Volkanovski is set to defend his featherweight title against Movsar Evloev.

Boxing has also been caught up in the uncertainty. Canelo Alvarez's planned October 31, 2026, fight against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh could face complications, with prominent boxing figures, including WBC champion Sebastian Fundora, voicing concerns about security following the airport attacks.

Meanwhile, tennis has already seen a major change to its schedule. The Six Kings Slam, originally planned for late October, has reportedly been postponed until December. Despite the uncertainty surrounding other sporting events, White has indicated that the UFC has no immediate plans to change its Middle East schedule.

Speaking at the UFC Edmonton post-fight press conference , the UFC CEO outlined his busy travel schedule and upcoming events in the region. He said, "I go to Abu Dhabi on Tuesday; I have like six events in the next 30 days in Saudi, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi."

White's comments came after Russian outlet Vestnik MMA reported that the December 5 Riyadh event could be scrapped altogether. According to the report, the rumored middleweight clash between Adesanya and Magomedov could instead move to UFC Qatar, scheduled for November 21.

The situation has also sparked debate about how UFC leadership handles staff safety when events are scheduled in areas facing security concerns. Ant Evans recently shared an account on X about the approach taken before UFC 120 in London back in October 2010.

According to Evans, Zuffa's head of security sent a company-wide email warning that London was extremely dangerous and advising staff to remain in their hotel at night. He also claimed that Las Vegas had recorded more violent crime that year than the entire United Kingdom.

Although the warning may have seemed excessive to some, Evans argued that it showed the company was taking employee safety seriously. He contrasted that approach with the current situation, raising concerns about TKO and the UFC sending staff into a region experiencing serious security tensions.

Ultimately, White's comments suggest that the promotion intends to stick to its current schedule for now.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois vs Moses Itauma is an all-British heavyweight rivalry for the future | 'British boxing's in a great position'
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois scored a stunning two-round victory in Saturday's rematch with Fabio Wardley to defend the WBO heavyweight world title; Moses Itauma has to rebuild from his IBF world championship defeat to Filip Hrgovic but can return to set himself on a collision course with Dubois
articles.body:
The sport in the UK has been dominated by the personalities and talents of Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury over the last decade. Although Fury and Joshua didn't box each other when they were both reigning world champions, they will finally fight in December in Cardiff.

That really will be a swansong bout for Fury and Joshua. While it's hard to imagine Dubois and Itauma matching the levels of fame Fury and AJ enjoyed, they can emulate them as two British rivals taking over the top of the heavyweight division.

They can also differ from Fury and AJ in a crucial regard - they don't have to leave actually fighting each other until the autumn of their careers. Both Dubois and Itauma are young, especially for heavyweights. Dubois is 29 years old and Itauma just 21.

They can fight in their primes, and they've got the time to box twice, even three times, in their careers if merited.

Dubois is riding high now. His two defeats to Oleksandr Usyk feel long distant after Dubois won an epic brawl in a first fight with Fabio Wardley to claim the WBO world title and most recently demolished Wardley in a rematch to defend the belt.

Itauma has to come back from defeat to Filip Hrgovic, a first professional loss for the fast-rising star.

Fighting for the IBF world title, Itauma outboxed Hrgovic, only to suddenly tire and unravel. Hrgovic, after absorbing punishment for eight rounds, stopped Itauma in the ninth.

Itauma now finds himself with questions to answer and a point to prove, just as Dubois did in his first career defeat when he took a knee against Joe Joyce in 2020.

Dubois is backing Itauma to come back and return to the heavyweight title picture.

"I hope so," Dubois said. "You need dance partners."

Frank Warren promotes both Dubois and Itauma. He believes Itauma will be improved by the defeat. "That's what makes you a better fighter," Warren said.

"He's 21 years of age. He'll have a comeback fight [in January] and I'm sure he'll come through it and then we'll look at all the various scenarios. But he'll want to be involved in it.

"What a great position that British boxing's in," Warren added. "This is not something that just happened overnight, we worked hard for this.

"We are on a mission to get these heavyweights under an umbrella but make the fights happen."

articles.title: Smith vs Puello: Date, ringwalk, UK time, undercard, weight, venue, records & how to follow
articles.summary: All you need to know about WBC light-welterweight champion Dalton Smith's defence against Alberto Puello in Sheffield on Saturday.
articles.body:
Dalton Smith makes the first defence of his WBC light-welterweight world title against former champion Alberto Puello in Sheffield on Saturday, 24 October.

The unbeaten Smith, 29, returns to his home city nine months after producing the biggest victory of his career by stopping Subriel Matias in New York to become world champion.

It is a homecoming which has been a long time coming.

Smith was originally due to face mandatory challenger Puello at the Utilita Arena in June, only for an injury suffered in training to force the fight to be postponed .

Dominican Puello, 32, is a former WBA and WBC champion whose only professional defeat came against Matias.

Can Smith cap his breakthrough year with another statement win? Or can Puello regain the title he lost in 2025?

All you need to know about the fight night is below.

Champion Smith dreams of Hillsborough after homecoming

Live text commentary will begin at 21:00 BST on Saturday, 24 October on the BBC Sport website and app.

Radio commentary from London will begin at 22:00 on BBC Radio 5 Live.

Stacey Copeland will present the live coverage, joined by lead commentator Ronald McIntosh, with Steve Bunce and former super-middleweight world champion Richie Woodhall providing co-commentary.

What time are the ringwalks for Smith v Puello?

Smith and Puello are expected to make their ringwalks at about 22:00 BST , although the exact time will depend on the length of the undercard.

The main broadcast is scheduled to begin at about 19:00 , with doors at the Utilita Arena opening at 16:00 .

Smith v Puello undercard & running order

Dalton Smith v Alberto Puello - WBC light-welterweight title

Giorgio Visioli v Maxi Hughes - vacant WBC International Silver lightweight title

Shannon Ryan v Emma Dolan - British, Commonwealth and IBF Inter-Continental super-flyweight titles

Edward Hardy v Ibrahim Nadim - super-featherweight

Aqib Fiaz v Jordan Flynn - super-featherweight

Joe Hayden v Will Harrison - welterweight

Connor Mitchell v TBA - super-featherweight

Chris Mulunda v Harley Collison - middleweight

Smith won English, British, Commonwealth and European honours on his way through the domestic ranks.

He travelled to Brooklyn in January as the challenger against one of the division's most feared punchers.

Matias had won 22 of his 23 professional victories by stoppage and Smith was fighting in the United States for the first time.

The Sheffield fighter elected to trade with Matias and, in a thrilling fifth round, dropped the Puerto Rican with a huge right hand before the referee stopped the contest.

It was the first time Matias had been stopped as a professional and took Smith's unbeaten record to 19 victories, with 14 inside the distance.

How tough a homecoming is this for Smith?

Smith enters with a perfect record of 19 wins from 19 fights, with 14 knockouts.

There are easier opponents to choose for a first world-title defence but Smith does not have a choice as Puello is his mandatory challenger.

The Dominican has 25 wins from 26 professional fights, with 11 knockouts, and has already twice held a version of a world title.

Puello won the WBA belt by beating Batyr Akhmedov in 2022 and later defeated the highly rated Gary Antuanne Russell to claim the WBC interim title.

He was elevated to full champion and went on to beat Sandor Martin before losing the belt to Matias by majority decision in July 2025.

Puello also presents Smith with a very different stylistic challenge to Matias. Rather than applying relentless pressure, he is a slick southpaw who relies on movement, speed and counter-punching.

Smith has long been regarded as one of British boxing's leading prospects, but victory over Matias moved him onto the world stage and a successful first defence would strengthen his claim to be one of the best fighters in the division.

It could also open the door to much bigger fights. Shakur Stevenson holds the WBO title, while Russell is the WBA champion. The IBF title is vacant.

There is also a domestic rivalry developing with unbeaten Londoner Adam Azim.

Azim is 15-0 and has been talked about as a future world champion, but Smith has, for now, moved ahead of him in terms of achievement by winning a recognised world title.

Should Azim reach that level, a future all-British world-title fight could become one of the biggest contests available to both men.

Promoter Eddie Hearn has previously talked about the prospect of Smith eventually headlining at Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough Stadium if his profile continues to grow, while Smith has spoken about wanting to build the kind of travelling support Ricky Hatton enjoyed at his peak.

Beating a former champion of Puello's quality on home soil would help show whether he can become one of British boxing's headline names.

articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski reveals brutal fight week challenge that has left teammates vomiting and injured
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski has revealed the brutal challenge his team puts newcomers through during fight week.
articles.body: Alexander Volkanovski has revealed the brutal challenge his team puts newcomers through during fight week. The Australian UFC featherweight champion admitted that the intense test has previously left participants vomiting and suffering pulled hamstrings.The challenge has attracted attention as Volkanovski prepares to defend his featherweight title against undefeated contender Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 on October 24, 2026, in Abu Dhabi. A teammate recently collapsed during the demanding session, leaving the champion shocked by the frightening incident.Alexander Volkanovski’s team challenge takes a scary turnAlexander Volkanovski’s team has developed a tradition of testing newcomers during fight week. The challenge usually takes place after the champion completes his training rounds. New team members must then take part in a demanding physical test.The 38-year-old explained how the tradition works and admitted that previous editions have produced some unpleasant results.redcorner_mma @redcorner_mmaID2112077714857529622redcorner_mma00“After I finish my rounds, the boys have a challenge. Every time there’s new boys to fight week, we do a challenge. It’s usually quite strenuous. It’s a pretty crazy challenge. We get people spewing. We’ve had people pulling hammies. We’ve had it all happen. Someone’s going to spew”, he said.The challenge often involves intense conditioning exercises, including work on assault bikes. These exercises can quickly exhaust participants and test their endurance. While the tradition is intended to push newcomers, its intensity has sometimes resulted in injuries and physical distress.The session recently took a worrying turn when one of Volkanovski’s teammates collapsed while using an assault bike. The incident was shared on the Australian fighter’s YouTube channel.Volkanovski reacted with shock as he watched the situation unfold.“Did he pass out?” he asked. “F– man, that was an absolute war.”The incident showed how demanding the team’s training environment can become. It also highlighted the risks associated with pushing the body too far during intense conditioning sessions.However, Volkanovski’s team challenge remains a tradition aimed at newcomers joining the group during fight week.Beyond training, the champion has also shown his loyalty to his teammates inside the Octagon. After Colby Thickness fought Vince Morales at UFC Perth, Volkanovski shared a replay on X and suggested that Morales had tapped during an armbar attempt.“I knew I seen a tap! #ufcperth,” he tweeted.Volkanovski is now focused on his own title defence against Evloev. The undefeated Russian has won all 10 of his UFC fights by decision, making him a difficult opponent over five rounds.The Australian champion, however, believes he has the skills and experience to secure a convincing victory. He has also suggested that he could finish the fight rather than rely on a decision.Volkanovski previously defeated Max Holloway to win the featherweight title in 2019 and defended it five times before losing to Ilia Topuria in 2024. articles.title: Dricus du Plessis targets UFC middleweight title return before making bold light heavyweight championship claim
articles.summary: Dricus du Plessis has revealed his plans to reclaim the UFC middleweight championship before moving up to light heavyweight.
articles.body: Dricus du Plessis has revealed his plans to reclaim the UFC middleweight championship before moving up to light heavyweight. The former champion believes he has what it takes to become a titleholder in the 205-pound division as well.Du Plessis wants to return to the top at 185 pounds first. However, he is already looking beyond middleweight and is confident that his size and skills will help him succeed against bigger opponents.Dricus du Plessis eyes middleweight comeback before light heavyweight moveDricusDu Plessis has made his intentions clear as he looks to rebuild his position in the UFC. The South African lost his middleweight championship to Khamzat Chimaev at UFC 319 in August 2025. Chimaev secured a unanimous decision victory to take the title away from the former champion.“I want to get my belt back and eventually go up to 205 and go test myself there. And I’m certain that I’ll be a champion. I’m big enough for that division, and I’m certain I can be champion at that division as well”, he said.The defeat ended Du Plessis’ reign at the top of the 185-pound division. However, he has continued to pursue his goal of becoming champion again.The South African returned to winning ways in July 2026. He defeated former UFC welterweight champion Kamaru Usman by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 281. The victory gave Du Plessis an important result as he continued his journey back towards the middleweight title picture.Despite his ambitions at light heavyweight, Du Plessis does not want to rush into a new division. His immediate priority remains reclaiming the belt at 185 pounds. He wants to establish himself as the best middleweight again before testing his abilities against larger opponents.A move to light heavyweight would present a different challenge. Fighters in the division compete at a maximum weight limit of 205 pounds. The additional size and strength could make the transition difficult, but Du Plessis believes he has the physical attributes required to compete at that level.His confidence also suggests that he would not move up simply to experience another weight class. He wants to compete for the championship and prove that he can succeed against elite opponents in a second division.Du Plessis previously established himself as one of the leading fighters at 185 pounds before losing his title to Chimaev. Reclaiming the championship would be an important step towards fulfilling his longer-term ambitions.His plan is straightforward. He wants to regain the middleweight belt, prove himself at the top of the division and then move up to 205 pounds.Du Plessis is confident that his size and abilities will allow him to become a light heavyweight champion too. articles.title: El morbo del Policía vs. Exconvicto de bare-knuckle termina en un KO brutal
articles.standfirst: El ex de UFC Jimmie Rivera dio cuenta de Brandon Meyer con una acción rápida y limpia
articles.summary: El ex de UFC Jimmie Rivera dio cuenta de Brandon Meyer con una acción rápida y limpia
articles.body: Jimmie Rivera, exluchador de UFC y Bellator, no ha competido en MMA desde 2021, tras su derrota ante Pedro Munhoz en UFC Fight Night 186. Desde entonces, ‘El Terror’ se ha centrado en el combate a puño descubierto y actualmente tiene un récord de 4-2-1 en Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC). El sábado por la noche, Rivera regresó a BKFC para enfrentarse a Brandon Meyer en el evento coestelar de BKFC 95 en Newark. Esta fue la séptima pelea de Rivera en el ring de dicha compañía y no le va mal. El luchador de Nueva Jersey logró su primera victoria por KO en esta promoción el pasado octubre, pero en su última aparición se superó, propinando un brutal KO de un solo golpe en el cuarto asalto. La contienda venía precedida de cierto morbo, ya que Rivera es policía a tiempo completo y BKFC lo programó contra Brandon Meyer, un luchador que pasó 12 años en prisión. Rivera incluso bromeó antes diciendo que Meyer podría darle una paliza sin ser arrestado. Pero las cosas no salieron exactamente así, ya que en el cuarto asalto Rivera acorraló a Meyer contra las cuerdas y le propinó un gancho de izquierda perfecto que lo envió a la lona. En bare-knuckle este tipo de noqueos están a la orden del día, pero sin duda la acción de Rivera fue muy limpia, al igual que la de Cole Cameron esa misma noche.

articles.title: Merab Dvalishvili: "Quiero romperle la cara a Petr Yan"
articles.standfirst: El peleador georgiano ha calentado la trilogía con el campeón de peso gallo antes del UFC 333 de este sábado
articles.summary: El peleador georgiano ha calentado la trilogía con el campeón de peso gallo antes del UFC 333 de este sábado
articles.body: Este sábado Abu Dhabi acogerá uno de los mayores eventos del año: el UFC 333. En esta cartelera habrá dos combates titulares, y uno de ellos será la trilogía entre Merab Dvalishvili (21-5) y Petr Yan (20-5) por el cinturón de peso gallo. Antes del gran día, el peleador georgiano ha dado una entrevista con Stake y ha mostrado las ganas que tiene de vengarse del peleador ruso después de perder el cinturón contra él en diciembre de 2025 y ver cómo se acababa una racha histórica. El año pasado, Dvalishvili fue el campeón más activo de la UFC, realizando hasta cuatro defensas de cinturón y consagrándose posiblemente como el GOAT de la categoría. Tras convertirse en campeón en septiembre de 2024, 'The Machine' logró defender el título ante Umar Nurmagomedov, Sean O'Malley y Cory Sandhagen. Sin embargo, Merab pecó de exceso de actividad y en su cuarta defensa Yan igualó su rivalidad tras pasarle por encima y evitar una gesta sin precedentes. Después de este tropiezo, Merab pasó de pelear cuatro veces en 2025 a tomarse casi un año de descanso, el cuál llegará a su fin este sábado para intentar recuperar el título. "Quiero simplificar las cosas. Quiero romperle la cara e intentar noquearlo. La última vez no salió como esperaba, pero creo que esta vez sí lo conseguiré", sentenció 'The Machine' en la entrevista con Stake. Además, añadió que "pelear contra Petr Yan es difícil, pero me he preparado muy bien y he entrenado muchísimo. Ya me he enfrentado a él dos veces, pero esta es una pelea diferente. Ahora mismo es el mejor del mundo y me estoy preparando a conciencia. Por si fuera poco, si Merab consigue cerrar la trilogía con éxito tiene claro a quién quiere enfrentar en la primera defensa de su segundo reinado. "Me gustaría enfrentarme a Song Yadong. Nunca hemos peleado entre nosotros y creo que es el siguiente rival más fuerte. Todos sabemos que tiene poder de K.O. Sería un gran combate, arriesgado y exigente, pero estoy preparado". En cuanto al descanso tan largo que ha tenido, Dvalishvili ha desvelado que no estaba en sus planes, ya que su intención era volver mucho antes. "Estaba preparado para volver a pelear en marzo. Tenía esperanzas de hacerlo porque sabía que nos habían dicho que nuestro combate no sería en la Casa Blanca en junio y que pelearía antes de esa fecha. ¿Necesitaba descansar? No, pero he disfrutado de este tiempo y creo que me ha venido bien porque he tenido más margen para entender lo que tengo que hacer en mi próximo combate contra Yan", finalizó. La espera ya ha terminado, y este sábado se saldará de una vez por todas una rivalidad que puede definir al GOAT de la categoría. El mejor grappler contra el mejor striker en un choque de estilos que tiene todos los alicientes para ser uno de los mejores combates del año.

articles.title: Cheavon Clarke vs Chris Billam-Smith: 'C4' set for all-British cruiserweight bout at Copper Box Arena
articles.summary: Cheavon Clarke and Chris Billam-Smith resume their rivalry in the professional ranks as the main event on Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on November 7, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Billam-Smith lost to Clarke in the final of the national elite amateur championships in 2016, a result which the Bournemouth fighter believes denied him a place in the Team GB boxing squad.

The British cruiserweight duo will resume their rivalry in the professional ranks as the main event on Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on November 7, live on Sky Sports .

But Clarke, who also defeated Billam-Smith in an English title belt series, told Sky Sports : "I beat him twice [as an amateur], but I haven't got any hook-ups on it.

"Maybe he has. We're professionals now and it's a new era."

Clarke went on to represent Team GB at the Tokyo Olympics, while Billam-Smith secured his ultimate achievement as a professional when he had a spell as the WBO world champion.

But the 36-year-old has admitted he is still irritated by his defeat a decade ago to Clarke.

Watching back footage, Billam-Smith said: "At the time I thought I had done enough to win it, but he's the aggressor, he hit me with some good shots.

"What I will say is the style there is a lot different to my style now. I look so frail and upright. It's very different to how I box now, but it was great, it was a great learning curve for me.

"But that was very much the beginning of the end of my amateur career. Obviously I had GB assessments off the back of it, but he got on and I didn't after he beat me. They were going to choose him on the GB team.

"It's hard to watch back but also gives me that fire in the belly."

Clarke climbed off the canvas twice before dramatically halting Jack Massey in his last fight in June.

But he insists his boxing intelligence along with his battling spirit will be crucial in the fight with Billam-Smith.

"I didn't learn nothing new about myself in Bournemouth," he said. "I know that once I'm in the ring or when I'm in any situation, you've got to stop me to stop me. If you get me down, you got to keep me down.

"Billam-Smith is notoriously tough, but boxing is not a game to be tough. It's not a tough person's sport. It's a smart person's sport, so we'll see."

Watch Chris Billam-Smith fight Cheavon Clarke live on Sky Sports on November 7

articles.title: Gatillazo de Dana White en el boxeo: libera a su máxima estrella
articles.standfirst: El máximo activo de Zuffa Boxing, Shakur Stevenson, llega a un acuerdo para abandonar la promotora sin haber peleado ni una sola vez para esta
articles.summary: El máximo activo de Zuffa Boxing, Shakur Stevenson, llega a un acuerdo para abandonar la promotora sin haber peleado ni una sola vez para esta
articles.body: Shakur Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs) ha rescindido su contrato con la promotora Zuffa Boxing que dirige Dana White sin haber peleado ni una sola vez. El campeón en cuatro divisiones subió al ring por última vez en enero pasado en un combate en el que dominó como quiso a Teófimo López. En los últimos meses se habló de un posible combate primero contra Conor Benn y recientemente se había vinculado a Shakur con un posible enfrentamiento con Devin Haney. De hecho, entablaron negociaciones entre ambas partes que no fructificaron. El habilidoso zurdo de Newark se queja de que lleva ocho semanas en un campamento de entrenamiento preparándose para combates que nunca tienen lugar. Así lo ha explicado el propio Stevenson: "He estado trabajando hasta el cansancio, manteniéndome enfocado, manteniéndome en forma. Llevo de campamento como ocho semanas preparándome para peleas que me dijeron que iban a suceder y no han sucedido”, explica el púgil. Prosigue así: “Este es el negocio del boxeo. No estoy enfadado con nadie, no estoy señalando con el dedo. A pesar de todos estos problemas y cosas que han estado pasando, he solicitado ser liberado de Zuffa Boxing. El fin de semana, mi solicitud fue concedida y ahora oficialmente soy agente libre”. Finalmente, Shakur abre las puertas a negociar con otros promotores: “Esta vez quiero decirle a los fans que mi carrera está en mis propias manos y estoy empezando mi propia compañía promotora y estoy dispuesto a trabajar con otros promotores y cualquiera más que esté dispuesto a ser serio sobre mi carrera como yo lo soy". Qué está pasando con Zuffa Boxing no lo sabemos, pero acaba de dejar escapar a su mayor activo.

articles.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Zuffa Boxing exit exposes further flaws in Dana White’s grand plan
articles.summary: Zuffa Boxing promised to “fix boxing.” Now its biggest star signing has left without throwing a single punch.
articles.body:
Shakur Stevenson has announced his Zuffa Boxing exit just 101 days after signing a reported "multi-fight deal" with Dana White's promotional outfit — all without throwing a single punch .

The news came via the YouTube channel of the unbeaten 29-year-old on Monday afternoon, pulling the plug on his relationship with Zuffa Boxing, seemingly, following the breakdown of a failed fight with Devin Haney.

The two unbeaten Americans had been circling a potential showdown later this year, but negotiations ultimately became bogged down by disagreements over the weight and a proposed rehydration clause.

It signals yet another blow for Zuffa Boxing and White, who promised to "fix boxing" when they entered the sport full-time at the start of 2026.

"I've been working my ass off, staying focused, I've been in camp for eight weeks preparing for fights I was told would happen but have not happened," Stevenson explained Monday.

"It is what it is, this is the business of boxing, I'm not mad at anyone, but I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing and over the weekend my request was granted.

"I'm officially a free agent," the WBO super lightweight champion continued. "I'm now taking my career into my own hands, starting my own promotional company, and I'm willing to work with other promoters that are willing to be serious about my career.

"I want the biggest fights available at 135 pounds or 140 pounds, where I hold my title."

Stevenson also stated that he plans to make a future move to the welterweight division.

"None of these guys can beat me. And give it a year or two, we'll get to 147 pounds," he said. "I will get there, but on my time, not on anyone else's. I'll be the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter soon and I'm open to co-promoting and working with any of the networks."

Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs), Uncrowned's No. 4 pound-for-pound boxer in the world . has clearly reached breaking point after a frustrating 2026.

The WBO super lightweight champion has not fought since beating Teofimo Lopez to claim the title in January. After signing with Zuffa Boxing in July , Stevenson appeared to be entering a new chapter of his career.

Instead, he has turned his back on White's outfit after the company failed to get a big fight over the line for him.

For a promotion that has consistently extolled a supposed ability to cut through boxing's usual red tape, it's an awkward early setback. Signing one of the sport's most talented fighters is one thing. Delivering the fights he wants is quite another.

White has spent years criticizing boxing's fragmented promotional landscape. Too many belts, too many competing interests, too many fights that should happen but never do.

His pitch was simple: Bring the sport into a more organized system, put the best against the best and use the resources of Saudi Arabia's Sela and TKO — the parent company of the UFC and WWE — to make it happen.

Stevenson was, on paper, the perfect signing to sell that vision. An undefeated, American, four-division world champion, one of the most technically gifted fighters of his generation. A man who had made no secret of his desire to face the biggest names available in boxing.

Yet the first major test of that promise has ended with one of Zuffa's most valuable assets heading for the exit.

Of course, there are always two sides to every story. And in boxing, there are often more than that — somewhere in the middle lies the truth.

We haven't yet heard White or Zuffa Boxing's side to this story, but if, as predicted, they claim Stevenson was being unreasonable with some his demands, financial or otherwise, it's hard to justify their hesitance considering the money they have already spent in 2026.

Conor Benn signed an agreement with the organization worth a reported value of $15 million for an appearance against Regis Prograis on the Fury vs. Makhmudov undercard, so surely the scope was there to overpay for one of the sport's biggest stars?

If money is the issue, it would be remiss not to cite the ongoing question marks hanging over Saudi Arabia's investment in sport .

Zuffa Boxing is not simply a Dana White operation with UFC branding attached. It was established through a partnership between TKO and Saudi Arabia's Sela, with Turki Alalshikh, chairman of the Saudi General Entertainment Authority, among its leading figures. Saudi backing has been central to the venture from the outset.

Saudi Arabia has transformed boxing's financial landscape over the past few years, but the question of longevity has always remained: What happens when the taps turn off?

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has decided to stop funding LIV Golf after its current season, prompting wider questions about the sustainability of its international sporting investments under its new 2026-30 strategy. This isn't to suggest that boxing is also imminently for the chop, but it wouldn't be hyperbolic to suggest that the honeymoon period Saudi Arabia's relationship with boxing is over. Welcome to the humdrum of marriage.

Spencer Brown, the longtime manager of Tyson Fury, told Uncrowned just last week that he expects December's Fury vs. Anthony Joshua bout to be "one of the last of the big fights" Saudi Arabia may finance. "Everything has to calm down," Brown said. "The money has to go down because nobody can keep paying that sort of money."

Whether Stevenson's departure serves as a red flag for other potential Zuffa Boxing recruits remains to be seen.

The coming months will tell us plenty. White has repeatedly urged the boxing world to "judge us on our body of work" after 12 months in the game. Well, as we hurtle through the fall, it is difficult to imagine a bigger story threatening to overshadow Zuffa Boxing's early progress.

For a promotion that promised to cut through boxing's B.S., losing one of its biggest signings before he's even fought under its banner is hardly the sort of work White had in mind.

Now, the challenge for White and Zuffa Boxing is this: Can they "fix boxing" without just throwing money at it? If it took just over three months for Stevenson to turn away, what exactly is this revolution offering — and, perhaps more importantly, what is it failing to deliver?

articles.title: Shakur Stevenson Leaves Zuffa Boxing Just 3 Months After Signing Contract, Last Fight Was in January
articles.summary: After just three months with Zuffa Boxing, Shakur Stevenson is leaving the company.
articles.body:
After just three months with Zuffa Boxing, Shakur Stevenson is leaving the company.

Stevenson announced on his YouTube channel Monday that he has left Zuffa (h/t Ring Magazine's Matt Penn ).

"I've been working my ass off, staying focused, I've been in camp for eight weeks preparing for fights I was told would happen but have not happened," Stevenson said. "It is what it is, this is the business of boxing, I'm not mad at anyone, but I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing and over the weekend my request was granted."

Additionally, Stevenson announced that he plans to start his own promotional company.

"I'm officially a free agent, I'm now taking my career into my own hands, starting my own promotional company and I'm willing to work with other promoters that are willing to be serious about my career," he said. "I want the biggest fights available at 135 pounds or 140 pounds, where I hold my title."

Stevenson, 29, has a 25-0 record in his career with 11 knockouts and has won titles across four weight divisions. He won the WBC lightweight title in 2023 and successfully defended it three times.

Stevenson's last fight came in January, when he beat Teofimo Lopez for the WBO and The Ring junior welterweight titles.

In July, Stevenson joined Zuffa Boxing, which is co-owned by UFC CEO Dana White, on a multi-fight deal.

"Shakur is one of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. He's 29 years old, undefeated and already a four-division world champion," White said after Stevenson joined the company. "This is a massive signing for Zuffa Boxing, and I'm looking forward to promoting this next fight."

Now seemingly set to represent himself, Stevenson said he wants to eventually move to the welterweight division.

"None of these guys can beat me. And give it a year or two, we'll get to 147 pounds, where is pressing me to be a 147-pounder," he said. "I will get there, but on my time, not on anyone else's. I'll be the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter soon and I'm open for co-promoting and working with any of the networks."

What comes next for Stevenson following his departure from Zuffa remains to be seen.

articles.title: MMA fighter receives big bonus on OnlyFans after suffering a wardrobe malfunction during loss
articles.summary: Lucero Acosta's PFL debut ended in a TKO loss, but a wardrobe malfunction during the fight went viral and resulted in a massive OnlyFans payday.
articles.body: A loss, no matter how you get there, counts the same in the record books. The reality, however, is that not all losses are created equal. Some are closer to the win column than others and some earn a big unexpected bonus due to a boob falling out and receiving camera time. The latter is how MMA fighter Lucero Acosta's PFL debut played out in Chicago on Friday night. The fight ended in a TKO loss to 9-1 Shannon Clark when the referee stepped in and stopped the fight. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! While the 32-year-old from Mexico did inflict some damage on her opponent during the fight, she was on the receiving end of a flurry of elbows that bounced her head off the canvas and at some point had one of her boobs pop out. Not all the angles of the end of the fight caught Acosta's slippage. This is one of the safe ones. The other angle, if you're really interested in that aspect of this fascinating story, can easily be found on social media. A tough loss by TKO in the record books for Acosta, who once went viral training underwater in a bikini, but a TKO loss unlike most TKO losses. As you would expect, the wardrobe malfunction that accompanied the third round stoppage also went viral. It then earned her that unexpected bonus. WWE STAR ADDS TO HER LEGACY WITH 'BUILT IN THE FRONT & STACKED IN THE BACK' EXPLANATION FOR LOCKER ROOM NUDITY In a moment of preparation meeting opportunity, Acosta said in a post on Instagram that she's cashed in on the attention thanks to her OnlyFans. "Extra payment on @onlyfans because we showed our nipples during the @pflmma live," she wrote. "It’s cute. Official sponsor." She then suggested that the "extra payment" might be as much as $500k. Not a bad bonus in a loss where, by the end, your head was being dribbled by the winner's elbows — if, indeed, it's anywhere even remotely close to that amount. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The loss for Lucero Acosta, her first by TKO, dropped her professional record to 6-3. It also ended a four-fight win streak that ran from September 2022 to April 2025. I think we've learned something from all this. You win some, you lose some, and some losses turn into a win of sorts thanks to a wardrobe malfunction.

articles.title: Ian Machado Garry Scheduled for UFC Return
articles.summary: UFC welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry is scheduled to make his return to the Octagon before the end of 2026. Machado Garry was last seen at UFC 330 in...
articles.body:
UFC welterweight contender Ian Machado Garry is scheduled to make his return to the Octagon before the end of 2026.

Machado Garry was last seen at UFC 330 in August, when he lost a unanimous decision to UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev in a fight that UFC president Dana White criticized the Irishman for a lack of action during the bout.

Just a few months later, it appears that Machado Garry is set to return to the Octagon to try to get the bitter taste of defeat to Makhachev out of his mouth.

Ian Machado Garry Rumored for Quick UFC Return

Per Ariel Helwani, Machado Garry will likely fight again before the end of the year, though no opponent or exact date and location were named.

Taking a look at the UFC welterweight division, there are several opponents who could make sense for him.

One potential opponent who has called Machado Garry out for several months on social media is Michael Morales , the undefeated knockout artist who is itching to get back into the Octagon, as he hasn't fought since a UFC 322 knockout win over Sean Brady, which was nearly a year ago at this point.

Though Morales has been linked to a welterweight matchup against Shavkat Rakhmonov, there is no certainty that Rakhmonov is healthy and ready to return after missing the last two years due to injury. If he is healthy, then he should fight Morales for a No. 1 contender spot at 170 lbs, as Carlos Prates is likely going to be the next man in line to fight Makhachev for the belt.

Another potential fight for Machado Garry could be a fight against former UFC welterweight champion Jack Della Maddalena, who hasn't fought since May, when he was knocked out by Prates.

Either way, despite a lackluster fight against Makhachev that White and the UFC brass clearly did not care for, Machado Garry is still one of the top-ranked welterweights in the sport today, and he will likely fight someone in the top five for his next fight as he climbs back into title contention.

articles.title: Is Petr Yan the Greatest Boxer in UFC History? Promotion Seems to Think So
articles.summary: Ahead of his UFC 333 title trilogy with Merab Dvalishvili, the official UFC YouTube channel has paid a special tribute to the Russian.
articles.body:
In less than a week, Petr Yan will put his bantamweight title on the line against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333. The rivals are set to complete their trilogy in Abu Dhabi, with both fighters having one win apiece heading into the decisive showdown.

Dvalishvili dominated their first meeting in March 2023, securing a convincing decision victory with his relentless pressure and wrestling. However, Yan turned things around at UFC 323 in December 2025, shutting down the Georgian's grappling-heavy approach to earn a lopsided decision win and reclaim the bantamweight championship.

With fight week underway, the UFC has found a way to celebrate Yan's return to the top. The promotion recently uploaded a video titled "UFC's Greatest Boxer ," featuring more than three hours of the Russian's best moments inside the Octagon.

UFC Honors Petr Yan With Massive Career Compilation Ahead of Merab Dvalishvili Trilogy

The tribute, posted on the UFC's official YouTube channel, highlights Yan's standout performances against some of the division's biggest names, including Jose Aldo, Urijah Faber, Cory Sandhagen, Song Yadong, and Marcus McGhee.

Yan's boxing is a big reason why he has earned such a reputation. The Russian uses a high guard to block and parry incoming shots while steadily moving forward. He also switches between orthodox and southpaw stances with ease, creating different angles for his attacks and setting up powerful body hooks and sharp counterpunches.

His numbers back up his reputation, too. Yan boasts a 55% striking accuracy rate, landing 1,456 of his 2,652 significant strike attempts. He also lands 5.16 significant strikes per minute while maintaining a 60% striking defense rate.

The Russian has recorded nine knockdowns at bantamweight, tied for the most in the division's history, and holds the UFC record for the most significant strikes landed in the weight class. Of course, calling Yan the UFC's greatest boxer is bound to spark some debate.

Fighters such as Max Holloway and Dustin Poirier have strong cases of their own, thanks to their striking records and performances against elite competition.

However, Yan's biggest strength lies in his technical fundamentals. Rather than relying solely on volume, he patiently studies his opponents, switches stances to create openings, and uses sharp combinations and intelligent footwork to cut off the Octagon. His defensive awareness also makes him difficult to hit cleanly.

Still, the UFC's bold praise might not convince everyone. Yan hasn't finished an opponent since 2020, giving critics another reason to question the label. With his trilogy fight against Dvalishvili just days away, the Russian will have another opportunity to remind fans why his boxing remains one of the best in the sport.
